title: Dequant scale-ordering regression in INT8 inference — investigation & stabilization plan
creator: Maya Chen
description: Summary: A subtle mismatch in the ordering of dequantization scale application between the model converter and the runtime INT8 attention kernels caused a small but measurable shift in token probability distributions for a subset of models. The shift manifested as a ~7% relative drop on our regression prompt set (conversation-quality metric) for two production models after the 2025-02-17 rollout of runtime-1.21. The incident did not trigger correctness failures but produced a sustained quality regression that crossed our alerting thresholds and led to a rollback of the INT8 default profile for affected families.
timeline: 2025-02-17 02:14 UTC - runtime-1.21 deployed to hosted with new INT8 kernel selection improvements
2025-02-18 09:30 UTC - Quality alert: conversation-quality regression >=5% on model redwood-chat-2-small over last 6h
2025-02-18 09:45 UTC - Oncall (Arjun) paged; initial hypothesis: kernel change or converter mismatch
2025-02-18 11:20 UTC - Traffic rollback: revert INT8 default profile for affected model family (hotfix), quality began recovering
2025-02-18 15:00 UTC - Deeper investigation started: reproduce locally with quantized converter + new runtime kernels
2025-02-19 07:10 UTC - Reproduction succeeded: small token-probability shifts in attention softmax inputs when using per-head dequant ordering
2025-02-21 18:00 UTC - Root cause confirmed: converter emitted per-channel scale ordering A->B, runtime kernels consumed B->A in one codepath introduced during kernel refactor
2025-02-25 13:40 UTC - Fix PR merged and hotpatch candidate validated in canary (PR #4386)
2025-03-02 10:00 UTC - Canary rollout to 15% and regression monitoring OK; full rollout scheduled and completed by 2025-03-04
root_cause: During a kernel refactor to enable fused MHA paths and support new CUDA heuristics, one INT8 attention kernel variant switched the assumed ordering of dequantization scale arrays (per-head vs per-channel). The model converter continued emitting scales in the original convention. The mismatch produces small multiplicative perturbations to pre-softmax logits; those perturbations are amplified in some prompt distributions and lead to measurable changes in sampling outcomes and evaluation metrics.
impact: Production impact was primarily quality regression (conversation-quality metric) for a subset of models using INT8. Some customers observed lower response relevance for specific prompt clusters. No data leakage or crash was observed. Rollback and hotfix reduced exposure within ~6 hours of alerting. SLA availability was not affected.
immediate_mitigations: Roll back INT8 default profile for affected model families (hotfix deployed 2025-02-18 11:20 UTC)
Lock runtime kernel selection to the stable legacy INT8 kernel for all models until reconciliation
Scoped canary to validate corrected ordering against golden prompt set before full rollout
permanent_actions: 1) Fix: Ensure converter and runtime agree on scale ordering; add explicit ordering header in quantized artifact format (done, PR #4386)
2) Add end-to-end quantized inference CI jobs that run converter + runtime and compare token-level distributions against FP32 golden traces (owner: Arjun, due 2025-03-14)
3) Expand canary gating: require KL-divergence < 0.001 and token-edit-distance < 0.5% across golden prompts before enabling any new INT8 kernel (owner: SRE, due 2025-03-09)
4) Harden kernel refactor review checklist: include scale-ordering tests and artifact format linting in PR template
5) Add telemetry for per-request kernel-variant metadata so we can correlate small quality regressions to kernel variants in production (owner: Telemetry team, due 2025-04-01)
6) Create a compatibility matrix for converter/runtime combinations we officially support and test daily
tests_added: Quantized E2E golden-run test (quant_converter + runtime INT8) - compares token-probability CDFs
Per-head vs per-channel dequant ordering unit tests in converter
Deterministic softmax unit tests for impacted kernels
Canary statistical check harness (KL-divergence, top-k token overlap)
prs: https://github.com/redwood-inference/converter/pull/229 - Add explicit scale-order header to quant artifacts (merged)
monitors: alert:quantized-quality-regression - triggers when conv-quality drops >=5% over 6h for any model family
followups: Arjun Patel - complete CI add and harden canary gating (due 2025-03-14)
SRE (oncall rotation) - tune alert thresholds and add kernel-variant correlation alerts (due 2025-03-09)
Converter team (Maya Chen) - publish artifact format spec and migration guide for model teams (due 2025-03-01)

notes: Lessons learned: small numeric convention mismatches (ordering, little-endian vs big-endian assumptions) can cause amplified application-level failures. Quantized E2E tests and explicit artifact versioning are critical.
Consider adding a lightweight 'smoke' comparison of token logits on canary traffic as part of rollout automation to catch these issues earlier.
Related: follow-up to ENG-20012 (kernel refactor guardrails) to add compatibility checks in CI.
